extracted.intended_audience: Prospective AAAI-26 authors and assigned reviewers (conference submitters and program committee members)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and procedural rules for submitting papers to AAAI-26 and for how those submissions will be reviewed (two-phase review, double-blind requirements, citation policies, and timeline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-phase review structure
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAI-26 will use a two-phase reviewing process. The abstract deadline is July 25, 2025, and the full paper deadline is August 4, 2025. Phase 1: Every paper will be allocated three reviewers. If a paper receives sufficiently negative reviews, it will be rejected without any opportunity for author feedback. Remaining papers will progress to Phase 2. Phase 2: Each paper will be allocated additional reviewers. These reviewers will not be given access to Phase 1 reviews until after submitting their own reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeline notes: author feedback window runs October 7-13, 2025; notification of final acceptance or rejection on November 8, 2025; camera-ready due November 13, 2025 (main track). The program committee and senior program committee will engage in a discussion phase, taking author feedback into account. Procedural implication: papers may be triaged in Phase 1 based on sufficiently negative reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 1 reviewer allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Every paper will be allocated three reviewers in Phase 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a minimum allocation for initial evaluation; sufficiently negative Phase 1 reviews can trigger summary rejection without author feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 1 summary rejection criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper receives sufficiently negative reviews in Phase 1, it will be rejected without any opportunity for author feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No further author interaction for papers triaged out in Phase 1; authors should ensure initial submission communicates contributions clearly to avoid early rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 2 reviewer independence
rubrics_metrics.description: In Phase 2, additional reviewers are assigned and these reviewers will not be given access to Phase 1 reviews until after submitting their own reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase 2 reviewers should form their independent assessments; Phase 1 reviews are withheld to avoid anchoring. After submitting, Phase 2 reviewers may see Phase 1 material as part of discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author feedback window (single phase)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single author feedback phase will give authors of papers from Phase 2 an opportunity to comment on all reviews (from both phases), running from October 7-13, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should use this window to address factual errors, clarify misunderstandings, and respond to reviewer concerns; the PC and SPC will take author feedback into account during discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind review (anonymity requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAI-26 reviews are double blind: neither reviewers nor authors should be able to identify each other. The first page (where the paper body begins) should include the title, abstract, content areas, and ID number (if available), but not names or affiliations of the authors. Acknowledgments of funding or assistance should also be omitted. Ensure that no information is included that would identify the authors or their affiliations; papers including such information may be summarily rejected at the discretion of the program chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical steps: remove names/affiliations from the submission, omit acknowledgments, and avoid any text or metadata that reveals identity. Violations can lead to summary rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: References to published literature required
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should include references to all published literature relevant to the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must cite relevant prior work; omission of relevant published literature may harm evaluation. Include full citations in the submission (while respecting anonymity rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing authors' previous work: preferred options
rubrics_metrics.description: When the authors’ previous work is relevant, they have three options, in descending order of desirability: (1) Use the third person rather than the first person (e.g., “Previously, Hinton et al (2006) showed that…,” rather than “In our previous work (Hinton et al, 2006) we showed that…”). (2) Avoid citing previous, unpublished work that would surely identify the authors (e.g., a previous technical report or PhD thesis which substantially overlaps with the current submission); such citations may be added to the camera-ready copy. (3) When neither previous option is appropriate, cite as “Anonymous (2019)” to indicate that a citation has been suppressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer third-person citation of prior published work. Do not include citations to unpublished materials that would deanonymize authors; if unavoidable, suppress with anonymized citation and include full citation only in camera-ready if accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on non-anonymous online material and reviewer conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two cases where the existence of non-anonymous online material will not be considered a violation of AAAI-26’s blind review policy: (1) it is acceptable for submitted work to appear in a preliminary version as an unrefereed preprint (e.g., on arXiv.org, social media, personal websites) or in any workshop that does not have archival proceedings; or (2) to be discussed in research talks, even if abstracts or videos of such talks are made available online. In such cases, the AAAI-26 submission should not include citations or other pointers to the non-anonymous material and the non-anonymous online material should not reference the fact that the work was submitted to AAAI-26; violations may lead to summary rejection. Reviewers will be instructed not to actively seek out such previous publications or to share knowledge of them with other reviewers but will not be disqualified if they encounter such information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your work exists as a preprint or was presented in talks/workshops, do not cite or link to those materials in the submission, and do not publicize the fact of submission on those pages. Reviewers are asked not to investigate authorship via such channels, but accidental discovery does not disqualify a reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timeline and key dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Key deadlines: Open Review submission site opens for author registration June 16, 2025; submission site opens for paper submission June 25, 2025; abstracts due July 25, 2025; full papers due August 4, 2025; supplementary material and code due August 4, 2025; notification of Phase 1 rejections September 15, 2025; author feedback window October 7-13, 2025; notification of final acceptance/rejection November 8, 2025; camera-ready November 13, 2025; conference January 20-27, 2026. Note: Deadlines are track-specific and may differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should plan submissions and revisions according to these dates and check track-specific CFPs for variations. Missing deadlines may preclude participation in the review/rebuttal process.
